content: During pregnancy, elevated A1C levels are associated with an increased risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends maintaining an A1C target of less than 6% (42 mmol/mol) to achieve optimal results. However, due to the physiological changes in pregnancy, such as increased red blood cell turnover, it may be necessary to adjust the target to less than 7% (53 mmol/mol) in certain cases.
